judgments.rationale: The proposal amends the summary of the paragraph (d)(1) access requirement to incorporate the civil proceedings exception from paragraph (d)(5), adding paragraph (5) to context_quotes. However, paragraph (d)(5) applies across the entire section and is already captured as an independent claim (C0007). Ingesting this separate provision into the summary of C0000 does not address any defect in C0000 and inappropriately commingles distinct statutory requirements without adding needed content.

The proposed summary asserts that an agency 'must require every individual, whether accompanied or unaccompanied, to furnish written authorization before access.' This directly contradicts F001, which states that 'the agency may require the individual to furnish a written statement authorizing discussion of that individual’s record in the accompanying person’s presence.' The statutory condition is permissive ('may require') rather than mandatory ('must require'), and it applies only to accompanied individuals regarding discussion in the accompanying person's presence, not to unaccompanied individuals.

source_spans.quote: (d) Access to Records.— Each agency that maintains a system of rec­ords shall—

(1) upon request by any individual to gain access to his record or to any information pertaining to him which is contained in the system, permit him and upon his request, a person of his own choosing to accompany him, to review the record and have a copy made of all or any portion thereof in a form comprehensible to him, except that the agency may require the individual to furnish a written statement authorizing discussion of that individual’s record in the accompanying person’s presence;
(5) nothing in this section shall allow an individual access to any information compiled in reasonable anticipation of a civil action or proceeding.
